title: A responsive virtual gateway has lost its only upstream path
scenario: R1 and R2 are a healthy IPv4 HSRP pair for 192.168.10.1. R1's priority is 110 and R2 is 100; both have preempt. R1's only upstream link Gi0/1 failed. R2 still has a working path and a verified return route. R1 configuration has no HSRP track command. Representative evidence follows.

exhibits.title: R1 HSRP detail
exhibits.text:
State Active
Active router local; Standby router 192.168.10.3
Preemption enabled
Priority 110 (configured 110)

question: Which configuration gap explains why the upstream failure has not changed gateway preference?
options: R1's uplink health is not linked to its HSRP priority.
R1 and R2 use the same virtual IP.
R1's configured priority is already below R2.
explanation: The group still hears a healthy Active router on the LAN, and R1 remains priority 110. Its failed uplink is not tracked, so that failure does not lower its preference. A tracking decrement of 20 makes R1 90 and permits preempt-enabled R2 at 100 to take over.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# track 1 interface gigabitethernet0/1 line-protocol
R1(config-track)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R1(config-if)# standby 1 track 1 decrement 20
R1(config-if)# end
R1# show standby
```
Use this object form on a supporting IOS image; the legacy interface form is an alternative as explained in the lab. Verify R2 Active and a real remote destination. Restore the physical fault separately, then verify R1 priority returns to 110 and routing works.

title: Two active routers use different HSRP versions
scenario: R1 and R2 should share group 1 and VIP 192.168.10.1. Their switch ports are confirmed in VLAN 10, both real addresses can ping, and the condition persists after convergence time. Each device reports Active with unknown Standby. These are representative excerpts.

exhibits.title: R1 show standby excerpt
exhibits.text:
GigabitEthernet0/0 - Group 1 (version 2)
State Active; Priority 110; Preemption enabled
Virtual IP 192.168.10.1
Active virtual MAC 0000.0c9f.f001
Standby router unknown

exhibits.title: R2 show standby excerpt
exhibits.text:
GigabitEthernet0/0 - Group 1 (version 1)
State Active; Priority 100; Preemption enabled
Virtual IP 192.168.10.1
Active virtual MAC 0000.0c07.ac01
Standby router unknown

question: Which fault is directly established?
options: Both routers must have identical real interface addresses.
Both priorities must be equal before any election can occur.
The peers run incompatible HSRP versions for the intended group.
Preemption must be disabled on both routers to avoid duplicate Active.
explanation: The version lines and virtual MAC patterns identify v2 on R1 and v1 on R2. They do not exchange compatible group Hellos, so each can consider itself Active. Raising priority will not repair the version mismatch.
fix:
```ios R2
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R2(config-if)# standby version 2
R2(config-if)# end
R2# show standby
R2# show standby brief
```
This scenario assumes version 2 is the intended supported design. Verify one Active, one Standby, peer addresses known, and successful client traffic before saving.
